crm_notes:
Summary: OrbitCode Studio builds an in-IDE copilot for enterprise customers (internal dev tools + customer SDKs). Primary ask: repository-aware context retrieval with low-latency streaming completions and strong residency/security controls. POC scope: ingest monorepos (private git), compute embeddings per chunk, store in vector index (prefer managed EU), serve context to a streaming code assistant with model/version pinning and fallback routing.

Highlights & quotes:
- "Need sub-100ms response for single-line completions inside the editor; 50ms ideal for snippet completions." — Lead Eng (Jonas).
- Very cost sensitive at scale: ~300K monthly tokens for active teams, looking to optimize batching and prefix caching.

Technical constraints / preferences:
- Chunking: hybrid — file boundaries + semantic split at ~512 tokens, store original file path and commit hash as metadata for provenance.
- Embeddings: open-weights preferred (cost) but willing to evaluate Redwood-verified embeddings if recall improves.
- Vector DB: preference for managed service with EU residency; fall back to self-hosted Milvus/PGVector inside VPC.
- Model strategy: pin a 13B open LLM for latency-critical completions, fallback to larger model for longer-refactor suggestions. Must support version pinning per-team and automatic fallback on OOM.
- Streaming: continuous streaming of tokens directly into IDE; must survive transient network hiccups and reconnect preserving context.

Sales/Procurement notes:
- Legal flagged data residency clause; procurement asked for example DPA language.
- Engineering wants an RBAC demo and API key scoping for per-team quotas.

Next steps (short):
- Complete POC telemetry run (Aisha to share telemetry dashboard link).
- SE to run 50-dev concurrency test to replicate target 50ms 95th pct latency.
- Legal to receive draft DPA and residency appendix by 2026-03-12.

Stubs/Links: POC plan (drive/orbitcode/poc-plan-v2.pdf), Fireflies ff-2026-01-22-6b3f, Jira RDW-1129 for KMS integration.
